did_you_know.text: Did you know? Jehu son of Hanani was the prophet who delivered the word of the LORD to Baasha. He reminded the king that Baasha had been raised from the dust and made ruler over Israel, yet he still chose to follow the ways of Jeroboam.
Did you know? The judgment decreed against Baasha’s house mirrored Baasha’s own actions: just as he destroyed Jeroboam’s house, the LORD declared that his own house would be destroyed.

Did you know? Jehu’s prophecy against Baasha and his house was not only because of their sins in worshiping the LORD, but also because Baasha had struck down Jeroboam’s house. Thus, the chapter emphasizes responsibility both for the deed itself and for the motive and manner behind it.
Did you know? Zimri was commander of half the chariot force, yet he managed to conspire against King Elah and kill him while he was drunk.
Did you know? Zimri reigned for only seven days. During that brief period, he destroyed the entire house of Baasha, but Scripture emphasizes that he too continued in the sins of Jeroboam.

Did you know? While Zimri was taking control of Tirzah, the Israelite army was camped at Gibbethon, a city held by the Philistines. When the soldiers learned of Zimri’s revolt, they made Omri king over Israel.
Did you know? Zimri died when he burned the royal palace over himself. His end is described as part of the punishment for following the ways of Jeroboam and causing Israel to sin.

Did you know? After Zimri’s death, the people did not agree on one king: they divided between the supporters of Tibni son of Ginath and the supporters of Omri. In the end, Omri’s faction prevailed, and Tibni died.
Did you know? Omri bought Mount Samaria from Shemer, the owner of the mountain, for two talents of silver. He built a new city there and named it Samaria after Shemer, the owner of the mountain.

Did you know? Ahab married Jezebel, the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, and did not content himself with the sins of Jeroboam: he worshiped Baal, built a temple and an altar for him in Samaria, and also made an Asherah pole.
